name: Act of March 3, 1881 providing for the sale of the remainder of the Otoe and Missouria reservation
aka: Otoe and Missouria Sale Act of 1881
promises: The remainder of the reservation in Kansas and Nebraska would be sold only with the consent of the Otoe and Missouria expressed in open council (section 1).
The land would be appraised by three commissioners, one chosen by the Indians in open council (section 2).
Royce records that the Otoes and Missourias were to be removed to a new reserve selected for them in Indian Territory.
today: The Indian Claims Commission ruled against the tribe on this sale in 1953: the lands sold for an average of $12.22 per acre, twice their appraised value, and the Commission found neither an unconscionable consideration nor unfair and dishonorable dealings, and that the tribe's consent was fairly secured (Docket 11, sixth cause of action). The Court of Claims affirmed those determinations on May 3, 1955 (Otoe and Missouria Tribe v. United States, 131 Ct. Cl. 593).

openQuestions: Audit 2026-11-08: resolved. The Court of Claims (131 Ct. Cl. 593, opened) heard the Indians' appeal on the fifth and sixth causes of action, the sixth being this 1881 sale, and held the Commission's findings supported by substantial evidence and affirmed them. The court cites the Commission's decision as 2 Ind. Cl. Com. 335; the collection's id for the opinion reads p355.
Royce area 626 (the new Indian Territory reserve) is grouped with this Act; how that reserve was later allotted and opened is a separate event.
The Otoe-Missouria Tribe's own account of the 1881 sale was not located.
